question.problem: Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{72}∼N(-1,{12}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $n=72$ from a normal population, what is the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}?$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n=72,\,\mu =-1,\,\sigma =12.
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(-1,\frac{{12}^{2}}{72}) \\  & ∼N(-1,2).\end{aligned}
$$
